items.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024
items.q: my main goal was to become a studio musician and so people like Bill Reichenbach and Chuck Findley and Urbie Green and, you know, scores of others but those come to mind right away

ctx.x: I’m wondering, about the time you were at Eastman and looking at it as a career, did you have this urge to do multiple things in the music business? Or was it a practical decision that came as it went along? Like opportunities came up and you said well I bet I can do this? How calculated was it?

Yeah that’s another great question, Monk. I think it was pretty calculated. I had a jazz background as a kid, my dad was a jazz educator at a community college out in California. So I was around it a lot and I played piano and I played drums before I got to the trombone. And you know I always just kind of wanted to be able to make a living as an instrumentalist even though my passion was certainly jazz. But you know my degree from Eastman was in classical trombone but that was back in the day when they didn’t…
You’re expected to play the part basically correct the first time. Is that true?
